chunks: ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from his father, from Ibn Faḍḍāl, from Yūnus ibn Yaʿqūb, from Abī Maryam, from Abī Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said:

“Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام ruled concerning one who pardons among those having a share, that his pardon is valid. And he ruled regarding four brothers, one of whom pardoned; he said: the rest of them are to be given the blood-money, and from him there is to be remitted according to the share of the one who pardoned.”

key_terms.أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: Imam ʿAlī عليه السلام in his authority as judge and leader
key_terms.ذِي سَهْمٍ: one possessing a legal share in the claim

ai.seo_question: If one heir pardons in a murder case, do the other heirs still receive their share of the blood-money?
ai.summary: This hadith records a legal ruling from Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام concerning multiple heirs or claimants in a case involving retaliation or blood-money. If one entitled party pardons, that pardon is recognized, while the remaining parties receive the blood-money proportionate to their shares.
